name: Shenzhen Megmeet Electrical Co., Ltd. (深圳麦格米特电气股份有限公司)
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: The verification point has arrived and it split. Megmeet's H1 2026 interim (27 August 2026) shows the AI-power leg working — power products RMB 1.841B, +60.92%, the only segment with an expanding gross margin (25.06%, +2.62pp) — while group earnings quality deteriorated: attributable net profit rose 45.21% but ex-non-recurring net profit FELL 16.13%, the difference being RMB 133.88M of non-recurring items dominated by fair-value gains on the wealth-management products holding the January placement proceeds, with operating cash flow down 84.62%. BACKGROUND: Shenzhen-based power-electronics and electrical-automation manufacturer, now organised into six business groups under current naming — 电源产品 power products (including AI data-centre power), 智慧生活 smart living, 新能源交通 new-energy transport, 工业自动化 industrial automation, 智能装备 intelligent equipment, and 磁电精造 magnetics/precision. There is no separate industrial-power reporting segment; industrial power sits inside power products. FY2025 revenue ¥9.40B (+15.1%); H1 2026 revenue RMB 6.061B (+29.68%) with direct overseas revenue RMB 2.180B (+45.49%, 35.97% of the total) and direct-plus-indirect overseas above 43% per the interim. About 3,400 R&D engineers, 34.6% of headcount, of whom more than 1,000 are AIDC-power technical staff. Founded 2003 by Huawei Electric and Emerson Network Power alumni; listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange 2017; A1 filed with HKEX 26 June 2026 for an A+H dual listing.
ecosystemRole: We assess Megmeet's ecosystem position as a power-conversion supplier converting an industrial base into AI data-centre power capability — qualified but, on the public record, unranked. Basis: the H1 2026 interim states in the company's own words that it is 「英伟达（NVIDIA Corporation）指定的数据中心电源推荐提供商之一」 — one of NVIDIA's designated recommended data-centre power suppliers — participating in the Blackwell and Vera Rubin power and HVDC programmes. That is membership of a set, not a position within it: the interim names no competitor anywhere in 238 pages and makes no share or rank claim. It is the only mainland-China power vendor NVIDIA has named for GB200 NVL72 power, and it publishes the full grid-to-GPU chain (edge cabinets rectifying 380–480 VAC directly to 800 VDC at over 1 MW per rack, a solid-state transformer still in development at a target above 98.5%, power/BBU/supercapacitor shelves, CRPS with 800 VDC input, PDB and Power Brick). Against Delta and LITEON it is the challenger in the same NVIDIA power-system-components tier; against the hall-edge specialists it is a rack vendor reaching upward.

productsAndServices.name: Power Products — AI Data-Center & Network Power
productsAndServices.description: Server/data-center power (CRPS/M-CRPS PSUs, power shelves, BBU and supercapacitor backup shelves, 800VDC sidecar cabinets, solid-state transformers), telecom/network power, medical power, industrial PSUs, LED/display power, and PV/storage/EV-charging core components. In 2025 the storage/charging high-voltage unit merged with network energy into a High-Efficiency Power business unit spanning data-center and storage high-voltage conversion.

recentDevelopments.headline: H1 2026 interim: revenue +29.68%, headline profit +45.21%, ex-non-recurring profit −16.13%
recentDevelopments.read: The half the dossier had flagged as the verification point. The AI leg is real — power products +60.92% with margin up 2.62pp, overseas +45.49% — but the profit headline is majority non-recurring and operating cash flow fell 84.62%. The company reports volume delivery to North American major customers began in Q1 2026 and names no AI customer.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess Megmeet is running an incumbent-funded pivot: the mature appliance-controls business (38% of revenue, declining) and diversified industrial lines bankroll the AI data-center power push. Basis: R&D held near 11–12% of revenue for a decade per filings, and FY2025 profit was deliberately sacrificed (ex-non-recurring profit −93%) concurrent with the 800VDC build-out.

(Moderate confidence) We assess its wedge into the Delta-dominated server-power market is architecture timing, not price: it moved first among mainland vendors on the 800VDC sidecar/SST full chain and is the only mainland supplier NVIDIA named for GB200 power. Trade reporting that it displaced LITEON as the #2 NVIDIA power-shelf source remains UNSOURCED and is now weaker, not stronger: the H1 2026 interim names no competitor and claims no rank, 36Kr's supplier account names LITEON as the second supplier with Megmeet the mainland entrant, and TrendForce's June 2026 800 V HVDC supplier note and DigiTimes' Computex 2026 AI-power coverage name Delta and LITEON without mentioning Megmeet. Treat the rank claim as a contested market narrative with no supporting source located; the recommended-supplier status and Blackwell/Vera Rubin participation are separately confirmed first-party and should not be conflated with it.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the geographic build-out (Thailand phase II, Dallas test lab, India localization, HK listing) is supply-chain de-risking aimed at US hyperscaler procurement — a mainland company packaging itself to be buyable by American AI-infrastructure buyers despite tariff and geopolitical friction.

(High confidence) The front-loaded expectation has now been partly tested and the answer is mixed. The 27 August 2026 interim landed: AI-adjacent power products grew 60.92% with an expanding margin and volume delivery to North American majors began in Q1 2026, but no AI-data-centre revenue line is disclosed at any granularity, order backlog is stated only as 「在手订单充裕」 with no figure, and H1 attributable profit of RMB 252M is roughly 30% of the RMB 832M FY2026 consensus carried on 同花顺 after the interim — implying brokers model a materially H2-weighted year. No published beat-or-miss verdict on the interim was located; the only 「略超市场预期」 broker verdict in the record covers FY2025 plus Q1 2026 and must not be carried forward to this half.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the EV/rail segment's doubling at 15% gross margin is a volume-share land-grab in commoditizing auto power electronics — strategically consistent (same power-electronics platform) but dilutive to mix. The durable margin engines are welding/intelligent equipment (38.5% GM) and industrial automation (28% GM), per segment disclosures.

relationships.note: The only mainland-China power vendor NVIDIA has named for GB200 NVL72 power; 800VDC sidecar co-developed.
relationships.context: Megmeet is a member of NVIDIA's 800V HVDC ecosystem — the mainland-China exception on both partner lists — and moved first among mainland vendors on the 800VDC sidecar/SST full chain: an 800V HVDC Sidecar for the NVIDIA Kyber rack-scale platform (>1 MW per rack, claimed +5% end-to-end efficiency, −45% copper) announced May 2025, shown co-developed with NVIDIA at OCP October 2025, and MGX support with a 110 kW liquid-cooled power shelf for GB300/Vera Rubin-class racks by May 2026.

relationships.note: Contested #2 fight for NVIDIA power-shelf share.
relationships.context: Trade press reports Megmeet displacing Lite-On as the #2 NVIDIA power-shelf source behind Delta — market speculation, not company-confirmed, and contradicted by LITEON's own record shipments. The two are fighting for the sidecar power-rack segment whose TAM independent analysis projects peaking around 2028.
relationships.source: Dossier competitive assessment — NVIDIA power-shelf tier

relationships.note: The ~41%-share incumbent whose server-power market Megmeet's wedge targets.
relationships.context: Megmeet chases a server-power market ~74% held by Taiwanese suppliers (Delta ~41%, plus Lite-On, AcBel, Chicony, Advanced Energy). Its wedge is architecture timing, not price: first mainland mover on the 800VDC sidecar/SST chain, deliberately sacrificing near-term profit for early position ahead of the projected 2027 rack transition.
relationships.source: Dossier competitive assessment — NVIDIA power-shelf tier

relationships.note: NVIDIA names Megmeet and Flex Power in the same power-system-components tier of its published 800 VDC ecosystem.
relationships.context:
Typed on the platform owner's own categorisation: both appear in one named tier of one named architecture, alongside Bizlink, Delta, Lead Wealth and LITEON.

The limit of the evidence is stated rather than glossed. There is no bilateral source, no matching product-announcement pair, and no ranking firm placing the two in a common share table.

The two are also differently shaped competitors. Megmeet contests the NVIDIA power-shelf socket as a power-electronics manufacturer; Flex arrives at the same socket as a contract manufacturer that has spent about $6.3bn since 2021 acquiring switchgear, cooling and power-conversion businesses, and has announced it will separate the whole segment into an independent company in early 2027.

policyExposure.exposure: As a mainland-China supplier selling into US hyperscaler and NVIDIA-ecosystem procurement, Megmeet faces tariff and geopolitical friction on China-origin output — the dossier assesses its geographic build-out as supply-chain de-risking aimed at making a mainland company buyable by American AI-infrastructure buyers.
policyExposure.mitigation: The build-out itself: Thailand phase II, the Dallas, Texas AI-DC power test lab (360 kW active, 1.5 MW roadmap) placing validation capacity physically next to US hyperscaler customers, India localization, and the pending Hong Kong A+H listing — on a manufacturing footprint spanning China, Thailand, India, the US, and Germany.

periods.commentary: Quality of earnings is the story, not the headline. Attributable net profit rose 45.21% while ex-non-recurring net profit fell 16.13%; the gap is RMB 133.88M of non-recurring items, dominated by RMB 137.35M of fair-value and disposal gains on financial assets — the wealth-management products holding RMB 1.65B of the January 2026 private placement. Operating cash flow fell 84.62%. Segment mix is where the AI leg shows: power products RMB 1.841B (+60.92%, 30.38% of revenue) with gross margin UP 2.62pp to 25.06%, against smart living RMB 2.557B (42.19%) with margin DOWN 4.33pp to 18.39%. Direct overseas revenue RMB 2.180B (+45.49%, 35.97% of revenue, 25.89% margin) grew at roughly double the domestic rate; the company puts direct plus indirect overseas above 43%. No AI-data-centre or data-centre revenue line is disclosed anywhere in the interim — the finest granularity published is the power-products aggregate. Consolidated gross margin is not printed; computed from the disclosed revenue and cost lines it is 21.21% against 22.07% a year earlier. No interim dividend. Next report: Q3 2026, due by the 2026-10-31 CSRC deadline.
